pointers.sentence: None of them is the framework: each is an ordinary application that a project lists in `INSTALLED_APPS` or leaves out, and each plugs into Django through the means a project's own applications have, but for the GIS application, whose config adds its `"geojson"` format to Django's own table of serializers (`django/contrib/gis/apps.py:GISConfig.ready`), and the static files application, whose finders and storage Django's default settings name (`django/conf/global_settings.py`).

None of them is the framework: each is an ordinary application that a project lists in `INSTALLED_APPS` or leaves out, and each plugs into Django through the means a project's own applications have, but for the GIS application, whose config adds its `"geojson"` format to Django's own table of serializers (`django/contrib/gis/apps.py:GISConfig.ready`), and the static files application, whose finders and storage Django's default settings name (`django/conf/global_settings.py`).

Where Django's core needs to know whether one of them is there, it asks: the `{% static %}` tag, for one, asks the app registry whether the static files application is installed before deciding how to write a URL (`django/templatetags/static.py:StaticNode.handle_simple`).
Each is a package under `django/contrib/`; the feed generator is `django/utils/feedgenerator.py`.*

| `"GET"` /bulletins/feed/ | 200, an RSS 2.0 document of three items | the bulletins' feed, an instance of a subclass of `Feed` (`django/contrib/syndication/views.py:Feed`) |

Its manager, `ContentTypeManager`, finds the row for a model class with `get_for_model`, which answers for a proxy model with its concrete model's row unless told otherwise, and makes the row on the spot if there is none; and it keeps every row found or made so in a cache held on the manager, by database and both by the pair and by the row's key, so that a later lookup of the same content type does not ask the database again until `clear_cache` empties the cache (`django/contrib/contenttypes/models.py:ContentTypeManager.get_for_model`).

The other way, `ContentType.model_class` asks the app registry for the model the row names, and answers `None` for a row whose model has gone (`django/contrib/contenttypes/models.py:ContentType.model_class`) ([Content types: `ContentType` and its cache](contrib/content-types.md)).

`ContentTypesConfig.ready` connects `create_contenttypes` to `post_migrate`, which Django sends for every installed application with a models module once migrate has run, and `create_contenttypes` inserts, in one `bulk_create`, a row for each of the application's models in the state the migrations leave that has none; the auth application's receiver calls it too, before its own work (`django/contrib/contenttypes/apps.py:ContentTypesConfig.ready`, `django/contrib/contenttypes/management/__init__.py:create_contenttypes`).

The `GenericForeignKey` has no column of its own: it is put among the model's private fields, beside the concrete ones, and names the two fields it reads (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericForeignKey.contribute_to_class`):

Reading a note's content_object, in the default fetch mode, takes the content type's key from the row without loading the content type, gets the content type by that key through the manager's cache, and asks the model it names, through the model's base manager, for the row with the object's key; the object is then cached on the note, and a second read sends nothing while the note's two fields are unchanged (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericForeignKeyDescriptor.__get__`, `django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericForeignKeyDescriptor.fetch_one`).

It is a `ForeignObject` that joins the lighthouse's key to the note's object id, with one more condition, on the content type (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericRelation.get_extra_restriction`).

`Site` is a row for each domain, a domain and a display name in the table `"django_site"`, and the question flat pages, redirects, sitemaps, feeds and the content types' `shortcut` view ask of it is which site the current request is on (`django/contrib/sites/models.py:Site`).

Either way the row found is kept in a dictionary of the module, under the key, the host or the host's domain it was found by, and a receiver of `pre_save` and `pre_delete` removes from it the entries under a site's key and its stored domain when the site is saved or deleted (`django/contrib/sites/models.py:SiteManager.get_current`, `django/contrib/sites/models.py:clear_site_cache`).

Either way the row found is kept in a dictionary of the module, under the key, the host or the host's domain it was found by, and a receiver of `pre_save` and `pre_delete` removes from it the entries under a site's key and its stored domain when the site is saved or deleted (`django/contrib/sites/models.py:SiteManager.get_current`, `django/contrib/sites/models.py:clear_site_cache`).

The function the other applications call with a request is `get_current_site`, which asks the manager when the sites application is installed and otherwise makes a `RequestSite`, an object with a domain and a name that are both the request's host and that cannot be saved (`django/contrib/sites/shortcuts.py:get_current_site`).

The first row is made by a receiver of `post_migrate`, which inserts example.com, keyed by `SITE_ID` (1 without the setting), when the table is empty and the router allows it (`django/contrib/sites/management.py:create_default_site`).

`find` asks them in that order for a relative path and, unless given `find_all=True`, takes the first match, which is how the harbour office's own notes/base.css, in a directory of `STATICFILES_DIRS`, shadows the notes application's file of the same name (`django/contrib/staticfiles/finders.py:find`) ([Finding static files: the finders](contrib/static-finders.md)).

Collectstatic asks every finder to list its files, less those its ignore patterns match, keeps the first file it meets for each path and skips the rest, and copies or links each into the storage the `STORAGES` setting names `"staticfiles"`, ordinarily passing over one whose copy there is as new as its source (`django/contrib/staticfiles/management/commands/collectstatic.py:Command.collect`).

The names go into a manifest, staticfiles.json, in the same storage unless another is given (`django/contrib/staticfiles/storage.py:HashedFilesMixin.post_process`, `django/contrib/staticfiles/storage.py:ManifestFilesMixin.save_manifest`).

The names go into a manifest, staticfiles.json, in the same storage unless another is given (`django/contrib/staticfiles/storage.py:HashedFilesMixin.post_process`, `django/contrib/staticfiles/storage.py:ManifestFilesMixin.save_manifest`).

With `settings.DEBUG` on the same tag gave /static/notes/harbour.css, because the storage's `url` hashes nothing while `settings.DEBUG` is true; with it off, a name the manifest lacks raised `ValueError`: "Missing staticfiles manifest entry for 'notes/missing.css'" (`django/contrib/staticfiles/storage.py:ManifestFilesMixin.stored_name`).

The static files application's runserver, which ordinarily replaces Django's own, wraps the project's handler in a `StaticFilesHandler` while `settings.DEBUG` is on or `--insecure` is given, unless `--nostatic` is, and that handler answers every request whose path is under a `STATIC_URL` that names no host by finding the file with the finders and serving it, without the project's middleware (`django/contrib/staticfiles/management/commands/runserver.py:Command.get_handler`, `django/contrib/staticfiles/handlers.py:StaticFilesHandler`) ([Serving static files: `StaticFilesHandler` and the development server](contrib/serving-static.md)).

`FlatpageFallbackMiddleware` and `RedirectFallbackMiddleware` do nothing on the way in; on the way out, each looks at the response, passes on anything that is not a 404, and for a 404 looks for the request's path on the current site: the flat-page middleware by the path without the script prefix or the query string, the redirect middleware by the full path, query string included, exactly (`django/contrib/flatpages/middleware.py:FlatpageFallbackMiddleware.process_response`, `django/contrib/redirects/middleware.py:RedirectFallbackMiddleware.process_response`).

The `index` view lists one URL for each sitemap and page, the `sitemap` view renders the URLs of one **section**, a key of the dictionary of sitemaps the views are given, or of all when none is named, and both send an X-Robots-Tag header and, ordinarily when every sitemap involved can say when it last changed, a Last-Modified header (`django/contrib/sitemaps/views.py:index`, `django/contrib/sitemaps/views.py:sitemap`).

Its `__call__` asks `get_object` for the object the feed is about, if any, and builds a feed generator, by default an RSS 2.0 one, from attributes of the class, most of which may be a value, a method that takes the object (for a part of an item, the item), or a method that takes nothing; it adds an item for each of `items`, and writes the XML into the response (`django/contrib/syndication/views.py:Feed.__call__`, `django/contrib/syndication/views.py:Feed.get_feed`).

Its `__call__` asks `get_object` for the object the feed is about, if any, and builds a feed generator, by default an RSS 2.0 one, from attributes of the class, most of which may be a value, a method that takes the object (for a part of an item, the item), or a method that takes nothing; it adds an item for each of `items`, and writes the XML into the response (`django/contrib/syndication/views.py:Feed.__call__`, `django/contrib/syndication/views.py:Feed.get_feed`).
The generator, in `django/utils/feedgenerator.py`, knows RSS and Atom and nothing of Django's models ([Feeds: `django.contrib.syndication` and the feed generator](contrib/feeds.md)).

Among what it does at start-up, `PostgresConfig.ready` connects a receiver to `connection_created` that registers hstore, and citext's array type, with the driver for each new PostgreSQL connection, by type numbers it asks each database alias for and keeps until `CreateExtension` clears them; and it registers the transform `"unaccent"`, and `"search"` and three trigram lookups, on `CharField` and `TextField`, for every database (`django/contrib/postgres/apps.py:PostgresConfig.ready`) ([The PostgreSQL application: `PostgresConfig`, operations and aggregates](contrib/postgres.md)).

A geometry field asks the connection's operations for its column's type, so it can only be created on such a backend (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:BaseSpatialField.db_type`) ([Spatial fields: the geometry fields and `RasterField`](contrib/spatial-fields.md), [Spatial backends: PostGIS, SpatiaLite, MySQL and Oracle](contrib/spatial-backends.md)).

GeoDjango loads GDAL as soon as `django.contrib.gis.gdal` is imported, and GEOS as soon as `django.contrib.gis.geos` is, which the geometry fields' module does; each is found by a path in the settings or by the names the library is known by on the platform (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/libgdal.py`, `django/contrib/gis/geos/libgeos.py:load_geos`) ([Geometries in Python: GEOS and GDAL](contrib/geometries.md)).
